title: Active Neural Matter: A Finite-Window Response Framework for Physical Systems and Distributed AI Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2610.14549v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Physical systems and distributed AI workflows can retain past information, receive delayed feedback and combine conflicting signals. These features pose a common modeling problem: determining what information about past interactions a state must retain to account for future responses. Active Neural Matter (ANM) addresses this problem through a finite-window response framework. Forward analysis uses each system's dynamics to predict state and output responses to perturbations, separating propagation from output sensitivity. Inverse analysis tests whether a candidate state retains enough information for these responses. With the system and future inputs or interaction rules fixed, distinguishable responses from histories assigned the same state identify distinctions the representation must preserve. translated_title: 主动神经物质：面向物理系统与分布式AI工作流的有限窗口响应框架
translated_abstract: 物理系统与分布式AI工作流都能够保留过去的信息、接收延迟的反馈并融合相互冲突的信号。这些特性提出了一个共同的建模问题：确定一个状态必须保留哪些关于过去相互作用的信息，才能解释未来的响应。主动神经物质（Active Neural Matter, ANM）通过一个有限窗口响应框架来解决这一问题。正向分析利用系统自身的动力学来预测状态及输出对扰动的响应，从而将信息传播与输出敏感性分离开来。逆向分析则检验某个候选状态是否保留了足够的、支撑这些响应的信息。在系统以及未来输入或交互规则固定的条件下，若被赋予相同状态的不同历史产生了可区分的响应，这便识别出了该表示必须保留的差异。这些响应在分布上的分离程度，给出了基于该状态近似系统行为的最坏情况误差的下界。不确定性界……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出主动神经物质（ANM）有限窗口响应框架，通过正向与逆向分析确定状态为解释未来响应所必须保留的过去交互信息，并据此给出行为近似最坏情况误差的下界。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Active Neural Matter (ANM), a finite-window response framework that uses forward and inverse analysis to identify what past-interaction information a state must retain to account for future responses, yielding a lower bound on worst-case approximation error.
